identity.title: Probing Episodic Accretion in Very Low Luminosity Objects

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present observations of line emission from N$_2$H$^+$ and CO isotopologues using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) in the envelopes of eight Very Low Luminosity Objects (VeLLOs).

question.value: Have VeLLOs experienced recent accretion bursts, as traced by CO snow line positions (N2H+ depletion vs CO isotopologue emission) compared with those expected from current luminosity?

evidence.quote: The aims are to search for evidence of episodic accretion using the position of the CO snow line traced by C$^{18}$O/$^{13}$CO and N$_2$H$^+$ emission.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit continuum and line emission sizes

method.value: 2-D Gaussian fits to continuum and integrated CO maps

evidence.quote: We fit the continuum maps with a 2-dimensional Gaussian function using the CASA task imfit.

method.value: Cuts perpendicular to outflow axis, width 4"

evidence.quote: The cuts cross the source centers and have a width of 4$''$, about $1-3$ times the beam size

analysis_steps.goal: Derive CO and N2H+ column densities

method.value: Optically thin LTE, Tex=10 K; N2H+ from isolated 101-012 component

evidence.quote: under the assumptions of optically thin emission and LTE with an excitation temperature of 10 K
Taking the isotopic ratio, $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O $\sim7.3$, in the local ISM

fitting.value: Hyperfine fits for optical depth check

evidence.quote: To derive the optical depth, we fit the hyperfine structure for each pixel (0.4$''$) in the N$_2$H$^+$ maps.

validation.value: Optically thin underestimates column by ~1.9-2.4, smaller than depletion

evidence.quote: the optically thin assumption will result in an underestimation of the column density by a factor of $\sim 1.9-2.4$

analysis_steps.goal: Abundance profiles and N2H+ peak radius

method.value: Divide column densities by H2 column from a spherical broken power-law core; average two sides

evidence.quote: We assume three core masses of 0.5, 1.0, and 3.0 $M_\odot$ within a radius of 10,000 au
The transition radius from static to free-fall is adopted to be 3000 au

validation.value: Compared with pure power laws p=-1.5, -2.0; range adopted as uncertainty

evidence.quote: This difference is taken as the uncertainty in this measurement

analysis_steps.goal: Model temperature profiles and CO snow line

method.value: DUSTY radiative transfer, CO sublimation at 20 K

evidence.quote: we use the one-dimensional radiative transfer code DUSTY (cite: iv99) to model the temperature profiles of our VeLLOs

assumptions.value: Gas-to-dust 100; dust opacity 1063.8 cm2/g at 8 um (Ossenkopf & Henning)

evidence.quote: Assuming a gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100 and a dust opacity of 1063.8 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 8 $\mu$m (cite: os94)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit burst luminosity with time-dependent chemical model

method.value: Adjust DUSTY luminosity so N2H+ peak matches observed radius; quiescent-burst-post-burst chemistry with deuterated network

evidence.quote: We adjust the luminosity used as an input for the DUSTY simulation so that the temperature profile leads to a N$_2$H$^+$ peak located at a radius $R_{\rm N_2H^+,peak}$

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of VeLLOs with past burst

evidence.quote: five to six VeLLOs with a past burst out of seven VeLLOs would result in a probability of 71% to 86% with an uncertainty of 17% to 13%
mass accretion rates during the burst phase of $\sim6\times10^{-6}-4\times10^{-5}$ $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ with a median of $\sim2.0\times10^{-5}$
a timescale of intervals between bursts of $12,000 - 14,000$ yr in VeLLOs

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of time in burst phase

evidence.quote: a protostar spends $\sim 5-6$% of the time in the burst phase

findings_qualitative.value: N2H+ and CO isotopologues are anti-correlated in five sources, tracing the CO snow line

evidence.quote: In five of the sources the spatial distribution of emission from N$_2$H$^+$ and CO isotopologues shows a clear anti-correlation.

findings_qualitative.value: DCE161 likely traces a transition disk

evidence.quote: The N$_2$H$^+$ and CO isotopologue emission from DCE161, one of the other three sources, is most likely tracing a transition disk at a later evolutionary stage.

claims.hypothesis: VeLLOs have experienced recent accretion bursts
claims.experiment: Compare N2H+-measured CO snow line radii with DUSTY predictions for current luminosity
claims.result: Five sources have snow lines at larger radii than predicted
claims.finding: ~70% of VeLLOs show recent burst signatures

evidence.quote: Excluding DCE161, five out of seven sources (i.e., $\sim$70%) show signatures of a recent accretion burst.

claims.hypothesis: Burst interval in VeLLOs differs from Class 0/I
claims.experiment: Burst fraction with 10,000 yr CO refreeze time

evidence.quote: suggesting that the interval between accretion episodes in VeLLOs is shorter than that in Class 0/I sources.

claims.hypothesis: Snow line radius persists after burst
claims.result: N2H+ peak radius does not change significantly in ~10,000 yr

evidence.quote: the radius of the N$_2$H$^+$ abundance peak does not significantly change in $\sim$10,000 yr

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: DCE065 depletion could instead be N2 freeze-out; DCE024 overlap could be projection or unresolved

evidence.quote: An alternative possibility is the freeze-out of N$_2$, the parent molecule of N$_2$H$^+$, in the high density central region
The negative contours in the N$_2$H$^+$ integrated intensity maps suggest that there is significant missing flux.

limitations_admitted.value: Hyperfine anomalies limit optical depth estimates

evidence.quote: Third, hyperfine anomalies due to non-thermal effects

referee_caveats_inferred: Snow line radii depend on assumed core masses and density profile
Outflow and missing flux contaminate CO profiles
Only 1-D cuts; resolution ~300-600 au cannot resolve post-burst inner peak
Burst interval conversion relies on assumed 10,000 yr refreeze time
